verdict.rationale: Fireflies' own AskFred assistant accepts natural-language questions across meetings and keeps context across follow-ups, but the evidence shows it only answers queries rather than carrying out commands. Natural-language actions such as sharing meetings or creating soundbites are documented only through the first-party MCP server, which needs an external AI client like ChatGPT. Missing for 10: evidence that the product's own natural-language interface executes commands or changes settings, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: AskFred is Fireflies' AI-powered meeting assistant that lets you ask natural language questions about your meeting transcripts.
Maintain conversations where follow-up questions preserve context from previous exchanges
some are read-only while others allow you to take actions like sharing meetings or creating soundbites.
The Fireflies MCP Server enables AI tools to connect directly to your meeting data without switching platforms or copying transcript excerpts.
